# Sattasatikakkhandhaka (Kd 22)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Following formal procedural inquiry, the assembly confirms that monastics are forbidden to accept money [SuttaCentral]. Scholars have frequently viewed the *Sattasatikakkhandhaka*, together with the preceding twenty-first Khandhaka (*Pañcasatikakkhandhaka*), as a later addition functioning as a historical appendix to the *Cullavagga* [Hazra 1994]. Textual analysis also notes that earlier Khandhakas are referenced within this chapter under varying designations, such as *uposathasaṁyutta* and *campeyyaka vinayavatthu*, indicating non-standardized chapter nomenclature at the time of composition [Sung 1999].
Full parallels recounting the council of seven hundred at Vaiśālī are preserved across the Vinayas of multiple early Buddhist schools, including the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mahāsaṅghika, as well as in Tibetan Vinaya literature [SuttaCentral; Bechert 1991; Banerjee 1979]. Passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the *Maṇicūḷakasutta* (SN 42.10) with its Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* counterparts (SĀ 911 and SĀ² 126), alongside the *Upakkilesasutta* (AN 4.50) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these correspondences through machine text-reuse analysis, finding significant matches between §1.3 and AN 4.50, and between §1.4 and SN 42.10, alongside extensive internal reuse within the Vinaya itself, particularly with the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), *Campeyyakkhandhaka* (Kd 9), *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Kd 10), and *Pañcasatikakkhandhaka* (Kd 21) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments are further detected by DharmaNexus in the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* and *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*, Sanskrit fragments of the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Chinese Āgama texts [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the chapter has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
